content:
Reports indicate that Apple will launch a brand-new "Apple Upgrade" leasing program next week. It is understood that, as part of the plan, Apple will gradually phase out the existing iPhone Upgrade Program.

iPhone Upgrade Program to end soon

Apple has touted the iPhone Upgrade Program as "the easiest way to upgrade to a new iPhone." Customers make monthly payments and can choose to upgrade to a new iPhone after 12 months. The program is backed by 0% APR financing provided by Citizens One.

In addition, Apple offers "Apple iPhone Payments." Also supported by Citizens One, the program lets customers pay for an iPhone in 24 monthly instalments, but without a built-in upgrade option.

The information comes from Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, who said Apple will "stop accepting new enrollments for its existing iPhone installment plans" as part of the Apple Upgrade rollout. According to reports, the scope includes the iPhone Upgrade Program and "standard installments."

One major difference is that the iPhone Upgrade Program includes AppleCare coverage, while Apple Upgrade does not.

It is not yet clear what impact this will have on existing iPhone Upgrade Program members. Apple Upgrade is reported to launch on July 28 in partnership with Klarna, when further details will be announced.
